title: Ten Years of $100 a Month Is Not $12,000

beats.say: Ten years of $100 a month isn't $12,000.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a crisp $100 bill resting on wet asphalt under amber sodium streetlights at night.

beats.say: Most people add up 120 payments and think their savings cap out right at $12,000.
beats.visual: Low angle silhouette of a lonely commuter walking past a towering glass skyscraper in blue hour fog.

beats.say: But invested at an average 8% return, that steady $100 monthly balance grows to $18,295.
beats.visual: High angle wide view of a massive empty industrial rail yard with solitary light poles standing in mist.

beats.say: That's over $6,200 in free growth without adding a single extra dollar.
beats.visual: Rain-slick street reflecting bright neon signage in a quiet deserted city alley at midnight.

beats.say: You might assume a short 10-year window is too brief for real compounding to work.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a figure standing on a cold concrete harbor pier gazing at open water at dusk.

beats.say: So what happens if you leave that $100 monthly habit running for 20 years instead?
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a long straight desert highway stretching toward a dark mountain ridge line.

beats.say: You put in $24,000 total, but at 8% interest, your account holds $58,902.
beats.visual: Dramatic low angle of massive concrete underpass pillars lit by a single cold fluorescent tube.

beats.say: That means interest officially contributed more to your wealth than your actual paychecks did.
beats.visual: High angle view of a dark quiet container port with towering steel cranes against blue hour sky.

beats.say: Now, what if you stretch that exact same habit out to 30 years?
beats.visual: Silhouette against weather standing atop a windy hill looking at distant city lights flickering in heavy fog.

beats.say: You deposit $36,000 over time, yet compounding builds your balance all the way to $149,036.
beats.visual: Cold neon streetlight illuminating wet pavement outside a quiet closed diner in early morning rain.

beats.say: Push it to 40 years, and $48,000 out of pocket turns into $349,101.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of heavy rust on an old iron bridge superstructure lit by harsh blue twilight.

beats.say: Small consistent amounts don't stay small when you let time do the heavy lifting.
beats.visual: Wide silhouette of a lone cargo ship moving across calm open water during a deep blue sunrise.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of wet asphalt reflecting sodium light outside a quiet train station at dawn.

caption: Saving $100 a month adds up to $12,000 in cash—but invested at 8%, compounding changes the math completely. Here is how small habits grow over time.
description: A breakdown of how $100 monthly contributions grow over 10, 20, 30, and 40 years at an 8% annual return. Learn the math behind compound interest and long-term investing.
first_comment: How much are you setting aside each month for your long-term goals?

facts.claim: $100/month invested for 10 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) equals $18,295 ($12,000 put in).
facts.basis: Standard compound interest formula FV = PMT * (((1+r/n)^(n*t) - 1) / (r/n)).

facts.claim: $100/month invested for 20 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) equals $58,902 ($24,000 put in).
$100/month invested for 30 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) equals $149,036 ($36,000 put in).
$100/month invested for 40 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) equals $349,101 ($48,000 put in).

loop_map.stakes: Ten years of $100 monthly contributions yields far more than standard addition.
loop_map.big_question: How much does a $100 monthly deposit really grow over 10, 20, 30, and 40 years at 8%?
loop_map.assume: 10 years of $100 a month equals $12,000 because short windows don't yield compounding returns.
loop_map.reveal: At 8%, 10 years turns $12,000 into $18,295, and 40 years turns $48,000 into $349,101.
